key_information_units.information: Headline financial performance for 2025 showed revenue declining 7% to €208.3m, gross margin contracting to 6.5% from 7.5%, operating margin falling to 2.7% from 3.6%, net profit shrinking to €2.5m (from €5.2m), and earnings per share dropping to €0.05 (from €0.12), with the decline driven primarily by a foreign exchange loss of €750k resulting from the Ukrainian hryvnia weakening approximately 12% against the euro during 2025.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Key figures section; Financial review section; Consolidated statement of comprehensive income; Note 13 (Finance income and costs)

key_information_units.information: Year-on-year segment revenue changes showed the Buildings segment decreasing approximately 10% while the Infrastructure segment increased approximately 10%, resulting in Buildings contributing 81% of total revenue (down from 84%) and Infrastructure 19% (up from 16%).
key_information_units.source_evidence: Key figures section; Segment reporting – operating segments (revenue tables)

key_information_units.information: The order book grew by 30% to €273.1m at year-end, driven by a nearly threefold increase in the Infrastructure segment order book; approximately 69% of the backlog relates to work scheduled for 2026, with the remainder spread across 2027-2028.

Cash flows for 2025 included €1.2m net cash from operating activities, €2.8m net cash used in investing activities (including €2.9m placed in long-term deposits), and €1.2m net cash used in financing activities, resulting in a net cash outflow of €2.8m for the year.

Liquidity position at 31 December 2025 was characterized by a current ratio of 0.93 (down from 0.94 in 2024), cash and cash equivalents of €5.3m (down from €8.2m), and short-term borrowings of €12.0m.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Liquidity risk section; Consolidated statement of financial position

key_information_units.information: Average employee count remained stable at 431 (274 engineers and technical professionals) in 2025, while staff costs decreased to €21.4m (from €24.1m in 2024), a decline of approximately 11.5% primarily due to lower performance-based pay.
